Round shipped: `980c088` — [telemetry lab](https://danfr4nk.github.io/attraction-guide/telemetry.html). Three fixes, all from your screenshot + JSON:

- **Thirds dividers were horizontal.** On your −12° roll they mis-cut the face by ~42px per end — that's the defect in the screenshot. They're now drawn perpendicular to the facial midline, rotated by roll around each anchor. The percentages were always rotation-invariant, so only the overlay changed.
- **Canthal tilt was roll-contaminated.** It measured in image coordinates, so head roll leaked straight into the anatomy read. Now reported in the face frame (image tilt + roll). Your IMG_0482 goes from +4.5° to −7.6° mean — and two photos of one face at different rolls will finally agree. The 24° L/R split stays as-is: that's detector noise on a conf-45 image, flagged, not fixed.
- **Iris scale gets honesty labels.** Per-eye iris diameters are now in the vector; L/R disagreement over 15% or yaw past 15° flags "mm scale suspect" in the quality box and the export.

One thing I found and deliberately didn't touch: asymmetry_9 at 0.6+ on both images is yaw foreshortening (−28° and +11.5°), not real asymmetry. De-rotating for roll would be precision theater while yaw dominates — that needs the 3D twin, which lives offline.

- **midline** — dashed facial axis, forehead through chin, roll-rotated
- **fifths** — the four vertical dividers splitting cheek width into the classical fifths, also roll-corrected
- **iris** — reticle circles at the fitted iris diameters with crosshair ticks and a Ø label
- **dims** — CAD-style IPD dimension line with extension ticks and a mm/px label, plus canthal-tilt arcs at both outer canthi with the degree readout
- **grid** — optional fine measurement grid rotated into the face frame (off by default)
- **scanlines** — subtle CRT texture over the viewer
- **rel σ column** — every metric row now carries a whisker bar encoding relative 95% CI width, so noisy metrics visually scream next to tight ones
- **Δ% bars** — the A/B table gets diverging bars, ±25% fills the track

Batch 1 results, blunt edition:

**3 of 6 usable.** The two fronts and the back passed with visibility 0.96+. All three profiles were rejected — correctly. In strict profile the far-side elbow/wrist/knee/ankle sit at ~0.02 visibility, pure occlusion, so the gate did exactly its job. No hallucinations, no mercy kills.

**Person-1 model built** from back + front: shoulder SD 0.009, hip SD 0.0025. The <0.2 bar passes with 20x margin to spare. Front vs back didn't even blink — the ratios are genuinely pose-stable across those two views.

**Holdout test surfaced a real defect.** The held-out front matched rank 1 of 1 (vacuous, single model), but the distance came out **4000.016**. Cause: with only 2 photos in the model, `arm_leg` had exactly zero sample variance, and the 1e-6 std floor turned a 0.004 deviation into a 4000 z-score. One dead ratio now dominates the entire distance. The ranking still works, but the magnitude is fiction until std gets a real floor (something like 0.005).

Still needed for full acceptance: your person-B batch, and ideally one more distinct person-A pose — an n=2 model is thin ice, as the zero-variance blowup just demonstrated.

Want me to fix the std floor and re-run the holdout?

Everything else sits at |z| ≤ 1.43. The floor did its job; the remaining distance is honest pose noise from mixing front and back in a 2-photo model.

3B into 3B — same key, 16 bars, that's a locked groove handoff. Then +2 semitone lifts (3B→5B), fifth drops (5B→3A, 3A→11A), and you shorten the blend to 8 bars exactly where the key jumps get wider. The bar length is doing the harmonic work. That's not fiddling, that's mixing.
